D2 · One origin, two heads

Like a biceps: all fibres start at one tip, run as one tight bundle, then part into two heads (5 fibres long head, 4 fibres short head). Coral bundle and long head, slate short head with cyan inner fibres. 32px master 3 + 2 fibres; 16px master near solid.

Variants tried

D3 · D fibres, one origin

Round 27 D fibres with one change: both crescent groups now originate from one shared point at the lower-left, like one tendon. The coral tip stays where it was; the slate and cyan fibres bend over their last half into it, and the coral fibres gather over their last quarter into the same point. The channel closes to zero there and opens exactly as before toward the upper-right. Open end, silhouettes, twist, fibre count, weight, tapers, angled cut and colours are unchanged.

Where the tips meet, variants tried

D4 · one origin, S-curve, tendon

D3 with two changes. The S-curve is back: the slate and cyan fibres keep their round 27 shape for the first 62% of their length, then the channel edge continues on its own round 27 arc, tucking into the coral hollow, and eases along the coral's inner edge into the shared origin. The outer edge sweeps into the same point in one clean convex curve, and the fan closes with its gaps open. Past the origin the fibres run on as one fine coral tendon, 9% of the mark length, tapering to a needle along the coral's direction. Open end, coral silhouette, fibre count, weight and colours unchanged.

C · fibres

C (M3 Half figure) in the D fibre language. The hook keeps its exact outline and becomes three fine tapered fibres that follow its curve and converge at both tips, with gaps widest in the belly. Colour as round 27: slate for the body, cyan toward the released tail (same cut), coral head kept as a solid circle. 32px master uses two fibres; 16px master is the original hook, solid, in three colours.

E · fibres

E (B3 Fan) in the D fibre language. Each blade becomes three fine tapered fibres that start together at E's single origin and fan out exactly along the blade, keeping its outline and its end cut on one angle; fibres are thickest past mid-length and narrow toward the cut. Colours per blade unchanged: coral = tension, slate = body, cyan = release. 32px master uses two fibres per blade; 16px master is the original fan, solid.

C · fibres v2

Three fibres kept. The slate to cyan split now slants along the hook: the cut follows the fibre direction, so the outer fibre releases into cyan first and the inner fibre last, instead of one horizontal line. The 32px master (2 fibres) and the solid 16px master use the same slanted split. The head stays solid; below, two fibre heads at the same size and position: A, three lens fibres running pole to pole along the hook's sweep; B, three fibres twisted into an S across the disc.

E · fibres v2

Fibres keep their full share of the blade to the end, so each blade ends in the original square cut on one angle, read as three fibre ends side by side. At the shared origin every fibre narrows to a needle over the first tenth of its length, so the nine fibres meet in one clean point instead of a knot. 32px master: two fibres per blade, same rules. 16px master: original fan, solid.
